claim: The UT Dallas 'When to Answer and When to Defer' framework (ICSE-NIER 2026) integrates uncertainty estimation, model calibration, and tool-based abstention: the model assigns a correctness probability, abstains when uncertain, and invokes lightweight program-analysis procedures to validate/repair abstained outputs, across both code classification and generation settings.
stance_target: downstream-utility mechanism for scalar code-correctness confidence via abstention + repair tooling
scope_conditions: code classification and generation settings, ICSE-NIER 2026 short/positional paper
quoted_support: Proposes a unified framework integrating (1) uncertainty estimation, (2) model calibration, and (3) tool-based abstention handling for code models: the model assigns a correctness probability, abstains when uncertain, and invokes lightweight program-analysis procedures to validate/repair abstained outputs

claim: Post-hoc calibration reduces probability misalignment but fails to improve ranking of predictions by correctness likelihood, echoing the same ECE-improves/AUROC-degrades failure mode found in DPRC's own base-paper SFT experiments.
stance_target: the ECE-vs-AUROC tradeoff finding that motivates DPRC's approach
scope_conditions: post-hoc calibration methods on code correctness prediction
quoted_support: post-hoc calibration reduces probability misalignment but fails to improve ranking of predictions by correctness likelihood -- echoing the parent paper's own ECE-improves/AUROC-degrades finding
